title: Pakistan Foreign Office Rejects UK Envoy Remarks as 'One-Sided'; Claims 52 Pakistani Civilians Killed by Afghan Cross-Border Attacks
detail:
May 2, 2026: Pakistan's Foreign Office Spokesperson Tahir Andrabi issued a sharp formal rebuke to UK Special Envoy Richard Lindsay's May 1 statement on Durand Line violence, calling the UK's remarks 'one-sided,' 'out of touch with ground realities,' and 'not reflective of the genuine security threats Pakistan faces from Afghan territory.' The statement represented Pakistan's most direct public pushback against a Western government official since Operation Ghazab lil-Haq began.

Critically, Andrabi's statement included a previously undisclosed Pakistani civilian casualty count: Pakistan claimed 52 Pakistani civilians had been killed and 84 injured by cross-border attacks emanating from Afghan territory since the conflict began in February 2026. This was a significant escalation in Pakistan's information war narrative, as it framed Pakistan as the victim of Afghan aggression rather than the aggressor in a conflict in which Afghanistan had previously dominated the casualty narrative (the March 16 Omid Center airstrike alone killed 411 Afghan civilians per Afghan IEA figures, and the April 28 Asadabad university strike killed 4–7 and wounded 70–85).

Andrabi argued that despite Pakistan's March 2026 goodwill ceasefire gesture and its participation in the China-mediated Urumqi talks, attacks from Afghan territory had continued — citing TTP cross-border infiltration attempts (71 killed in Hassan Khel, North Waziristan, April 25–27) and Afghan Taliban artillery fire into South Waziristan (injuring 5 Pakistani civilians April 29–30). Pakistan urged the international community to take 'a balanced, fact-based view' of the conflict rather than what it characterized as reflexively accepting Taliban claims about civilian casualties.

The statement drew a stark contrast with the Afghan Taliban's framing of the same conflict. Taliban Deputy Spokesman Fitrat had accused Pakistan of 'war crimes against civilians and educational institutions' for the April 28 university strike, while Pakistan's Foreign Office described itself as exercising restrained self-defense against persistent terrorism from Afghan soil. The competing casualty narratives — Afghanistan with internationally-confirmed civilian deaths in the hundreds from Pakistani strikes, Pakistan with 52 claimed civilian deaths from Afghan cross-border attacks — reflected the fundamental information war dimension of the Af-Pak conflict in which both sides contest the basic facts of responsibility for civilian harm.

media.caption: Pakistan Foreign Office fires back at UK envoy: calls remarks 'one-sided,' claims 52 Pakistani civilians killed and 84 injured by cross-border Afghan attacks
